name: Payment card visual
purpose: A passive representation of a PHYSICAL PAYMENT INSTRUMENT — the card face, at ID-1 proportions, showing which piece of plastic this is and whether it is usable right now. Product name, masked number, cardholder, expiry, a contactless indicator, and a status chip carrying a word. It carries NO balance, deliberately. PROPOSED #204 (itinerary row 93, slug payment-card-visual) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).
$intent-parked: PARKED #209 (Dave, live: 'Park it but we need to follow up it needs an intent, we need a follow-up'). The authored value was 'identity' — an unruled word the s195-D1 gate refused (legal set: change-over-time, comparison, composition, distribution, relationship; a word enters only by Dave's ruling). The live `intent` field is withdrawn so the address no longer dangles; the component still NEEDS an intent and the follow-up is store row W-58. Restore as `intent` when Dave rules the word.

props.name: productName
props.$note: Rendered in the Tags atom (square outline), copied from Tags.reference via Account-card. E.g. 'Business debit'.

props.name: maskedNumber
props.$note: DEFAULT STATE. Uses Account-card's own ··· masking idiom, copied verbatim — no new mask glyph was introduced.

props.name: revealed
props.$note: Shows the full PAN. The specimen uses 4000 0000 0000 4821, the ISO/IEC 7812 test range. Drawing the state is NOT an endorsement of showing a PAN in production UI.

props.name: contactless
props.$note: Renders the REAL library glyph assets/icons/media/contactless.svg, byte-matched via <symbol>. A functional indicator, not a brand mark.

props.name: status
props.$note: Rendered as a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip ALWAYS CARRYING ITS WORD. Which status maps to which chip tint is a SEMANTIC binding and is DAVE'S — proposed, not ruled.

props.name: size
props.$note: 340px and 240px wide; aspect-ratio is fixed at 1.586 in both.

props.name: issuerMark
props.$note: ⛔ DECLARED, EMPTY, PROPOSED PLACEHOLDER. Not drawn — see antiPatterns and knownFindings.

props.name: networkMark
props.$note: ⛔ DECLARED, EMPTY, PROPOSED PLACEHOLDER. Card-network artwork is licensed and governed outside this system.

props.name: chip
props.$note: ⛔ DECLARED, EMPTY, PROPOSED PLACEHOLDER. No EMV chip glyph exists in the HSBC library (probe quoted below) and authoring one inline would be an invented icon.

variants.name: default
variants.use: A single card in a card-management view, 340px.

variants.name: compact
variants.use: A wallet list or a card picker row, 240px.

variants.name: revealed
variants.use: The number-shown state, behind an explicit 44px control.

variants.name: unusable
variants.use: Frozen or expired. The chip word is the carrier; the face also drops to alpha/48, a second non-colour channel.

tokens.surface: tertiary/background/default — #FFFFFF | #1F1F1F. The SAME surface Account-card binds, copied. See the inverse-surface finding for why there is no dark card face.
tokens.muted: text/secondary — the contactless glyph and the placeholder slot labels
tokens.slotBorder: form/border/default #808080 — 3.95:1 on white, 4.17:1 on the dark surface (measured #204), so the dashed placeholder outline is itself a legible non-text mark
tokens.status: rag/success + rag/success-tint | rag/warning + rag/warning-tint — copied byte-for-byte from Account-card
tokens.control: button/tertiary/{label,border,background-hover}/default @ .t-cm-button, 44px tall — Button.reference's tertiary tier, copied verbatim
tokens.radius: border-radius/surface (card shell) + border-radius/indicator (tag, chip, slots) + border-radius/control (button). 0 in Mono and Legacy; Console forks surface to 20px through the cascade.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value here already exists and is already bound by a gated component.

motion.hover: Only on the reveal control — the tertiary button's background tint. No scale physics copied: the card face itself is not a control.

responsive.rule: Fixed width per size (340 / 240) with aspect-ratio 1.586 = ID-1 (ISO/IEC 7810, 85.60×53.98 mm). Cards wrap in a flex rack rather than scaling; the PHYSICAL proportion must not distort. Verified at 1400px and 480px.

mustNotNeighbour: An Account-card for the SAME product shown as a card face (two components claiming to be the same object)

accessibility.role: role="group" + aria-labelledby, copied from Account-card, so AT announces the card as one unit.
accessibility.name: The card's own descriptive line ('Business debit card, ending 4821') is the labelled element. In the revealed state that element holds the PAN, so the accessible name and the on-screen value are the same object.
accessibility.placeholders: ⛔ The three brand placeholder slots are aria-hidden="true". They are scaffolding for the reviewer's eye, not content, and must never be announced.
accessibility.contactless: The glyph is aria-hidden; a visually-hidden 'Contactless enabled' span carries the meaning in text.
accessibility.notColourAlone: Every status carries its WORD in the chip ('Active', 'Frozen by you', 'Expired 08/25'). The unusable states additionally drop to alpha/48 — a second non-colour channel. No state on this card is signalled by hue alone (1.4.1).
accessibility.hitArea: The reveal button is 44px tall by the Button token. MEASURED BY HAND at #204 in all four themes, both modes — NO GATE READS the 44px minimum-hit-area token from a snippet.
accessibility.keyboard: The reveal button is a real <button> with aria-pressed. The card face is passive and is NOT in the tab order.

antiPatterns: ⛔ DRAWING A CARD-NETWORK MARK, AN ISSUER LOGOTYPE, AN EMV CHIP PATTERN OR ANY EMBOSSING. That artwork is licensed and governed outside this design system, and #86-D2 fences our own marks too ('the crescent is only a mark for apollo … use the hsbc mark normally'). Probe, quoted: `ls knowledge/assets/icons/**/ | grep -iE "chip|visa|mastercard|amex|network"` → EMPTY. The slots exist to be FILLED with real assets, never to be improvised.
Showing a BALANCE on the card face. That is Account-card's job; a payment-card visual with a balance is an Account-card wearing a card shape.
Showing the full PAN by default. The masked form is the default; revealing is an explicit user act behind a 44px control.
Building a card BACK (magstripe, signature panel, CVV) here — those are secure-data surfaces (see Secure-entry) wrapped in licensed brand furniture.

Inventing a dark or 'premium' card face by hardcoding a charcoal. The inverse/hero surface role DOES NOT EXIST yet and _COMPONENT-GAPS.md already records that the fitness-test portfolio invented #0E1014 for exactly this reason. Mint the role first.
Adding a gradient, a shadow or a metallic treatment — the brand stays flat and angular.
Making the card face itself clickable. If the card is a target, wrap it in the approved interactive row (List-items) rather than growing a click handler on a passive object.
Relying on the status DOT to convey state. The dot is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204); the word is the carrier.

$differsFrom.Account-card: Account-card's subject is MONEY (label + masked number + BALANCE + status chip). This component's subject is the physical INSTRUMENT and carries no balance at all. Account-card answers 'how much is in it?'; this answers 'which piece of plastic is this, and is it usable right now?'. Every shared atom — shell, ··· masking idiom, Tags atom, RAG chip — is COPIED from Account-card and was not re-drawn.
$differsFrom.Cards: Cards is the generic content-surface family: a rectangle you put arbitrary things in, with no anatomy. This is a representation of a specific real-world object with a fixed ID-1 geometry and a fixed anatomy. Cards has no anatomy; this is nothing but anatomy.
$differsFrom.Chart-bullet: No relationship whatsoever. Nothing on this card is a measure, a target or a quantity. Named here only because the itinerary places rows 93 and 94 adjacent and a reader may carry row 94's chart neighbourhood across.

$decisionsForDave: Should this component exist at all in this form? Fintech semantics are yours.
The three brand placeholder slots: right shape, right positions, right count? And is a dashed labelled placeholder the right way to say 'a licensed asset belongs here'?

Corners. The card follows the angular rule (square in Mono/Legacy, 20px in Console). Real cards are rounded. Should a payment-card visual be a documented EXEMPTION from the angular rule, like Avatar and Badge?
The dark / premium card face. It needs the inverse/hero surface role that _COMPONENT-GAPS.md records as missing. Mint it, or accept a light-only card face?

The status vocabulary and its chip binding: active → success tint, frozen → warning tint, expired → warning tint. Should 'expired' be the error seat instead? That touches the two-red law and is deliberately not taken here.
The reveal control: text button ('Show number') rather than an icon, because no eye/reveal glyph exists in the library. Correct call, or is a new glyph owed to _ICON-GAPS.md?
Should the revealed-PAN state ship at all, or should the component stop at masked?
